messages:
nina: I hacked together a different handoff idea: 'lease escrow'. Instead of immediate transfer we create an escrow record that both sender and receiver can read/write. escrow holds transfer_id, target, epoch, and state (proposed/accepted/committed). Intent: make recovery deterministic after partitions and reduce racing with eviction.

leo: escrow record = single source of truth? where is it stored? datacenter-local persistent KV?

nina: yes, store escrow in local durable small DB (append-only log per-shard). Sender writes PROPOSE, waits for receiver ACCEPT, then COMMIT. All actions are idempotent via transfer_id. If sender crashes, coordinator can consult escrow to decide.

chris: how do reads behave while escrow is pending? we need read-after-write guarantees.

nina: policy: sender marks prefix as read-protected while escrow is pending (fast path: allow stale shadow-reads tagged with warning). Writes routed to receiver buffer once ACCEPT seen. This keeps user visible correctness.

dave: sounds safer but extra durable write per handoff. any perf numbers?

nina: microbench on toy cluster: durable PROPOSE write adds ~200us median. COMMIT adds ~180us. With batching proposals every 3ms we amortize cost; net increase in p50 ~120us, p99 ~1.8ms for heavy handoffs.

leo: failure modes? if escrow lost or DB corrupt, will we lose ownership info?

nina: escrow DB is replicated with Paxos within shard pool. Also include checksums + signed entries so restore can validate. If escrow is unavailable, fallback is coordinator forced assignment using monotonic epoch.

chris: eviction interplay: can eviction remove keys while escrow pending?

nina: eviction must consult escrow: eviction attempts check escrow state; if PROPOSED, we defer eviction until either COMMIT or reclaim timeout. Reclaim timeout uses exponential backoff and tenant credits to avoid thrash.

dave: metrics: please emit `escrow.proposed`, `escrow.accepted`, `escrow.committed`, `escrow.reclaimed`, and tracing span `handoff.escrow` with transfer_id. Also add per-shard slow-path counters for deferred-evictions.

ops-bot: suggested canary: us-east-1, 4% traffic, 24h watch, feature-flag `handoff.escrow=true`.

leo: compatibility: cluster mix ok? escrow requires shard-pool membership version >=v3. We'll gate by per-shard feature-flag.

chris: tests: unit for idempotency, integration with escrow DB replication, chaos where escrow acceptor loses disk for a bit, and hotkey load tests to verify p99.

nina: noted. I'll add reclaim policy: reclaim after 1500ms + jitter, 2 retries, then mark ownerless and route to coordinator for forced commit. Also include a safepoint when ownerless to prevent writes for 10s unless coordinator reassigns.

dave: +1 but keep ownerless windows short. Ops needs automated alert on ownerless event.

nina: will add alert and dashboard. plan: design doc -> unit tests -> integration -> canary. tagging @leo @chris for review. small sync tomorrow 11:00 PT to pair on chaos tests.

chris: ack, will review.

nina: thanks all :thumbsup:
